clue.text: A friend is, in part, a supporter of the pontiff

indicators.note: the words before are placed inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a friend as being partly a fan of the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'in part' read as 'partly'; the word 'in' is really the container signal and 'part' its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A papalist is an advocate of papal authority, a backer of the Pope.

clue.text: Fish with rod -—— it's plain, one says

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: An angler with a fishing rod remarks on how simple it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'plain as a pikestaff' means obvious, so the word is what one compares plainness to.

clue.text: I'm absorbed by old English hobby

indicators.note: the first piece is soaked up inside the following ones

parts.note: past means former or old

explanation.surface: Someone says they are engrossed in an old English pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' places the pronoun just before the final E, splitting old from English.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is an activity done for pleasure, a hobby.

clue.text: Pass up beer in this place

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An invitation to pass the beer round at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass up' looks like 'decline'; 'up' turns COL into LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a place or setting where something happens.

clue.text: Tatty underclothes abandoned by the rogue

indicators.note: shabby and worn, so the letters are jumbled; the letters of 'the' are abandoned from the pool

explanation.surface: A villain discards his shabby underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Take THE away from UNDERCLOTHES, as 'abandoned by' says, and rearrange the rest (UNDERCLOS).
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rascal, a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Instructions referring to cold, crumbly pie?

parts.note: re is a common short form meaning concerning or regarding
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: a crumbly thing falls apart, so the letters of the next word break up and rearrange

explanation.surface: Directions for making a cold pie with crumbly pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbly' turns PIE into IPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of cooking directions, so a set of instructions.

clue.text: Brazilian city, in our opinion, is wild and unruly

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil
to us means as we see it

explanation.surface: We think Rio de Janeiro is a wild, lawless place.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means disorderly and boisterous, so out of control.

clue.text: Called solicitor after policeman avoided duty

indicators.note: called means spoken aloud, so what follows is heard

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits business; it comes after cop, a policeman

explanation.surface: A policeman shirked his duty and then phoned his lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer; it is a tout. 'Cop tout' spoken sounds like the answer, whose 'copped' is said 'copt'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is to dodge a responsibility, so copped out means shirked.

clue.text: Lacking water, camper is to boil sweet-smelling liquid

indicators.note: the camper is missing the next piece, so those letters go

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
to fume is to seethe or boil with anger

explanation.surface: A camper with no water boils something fragrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CAM, a river, from CAMPER to leave PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume is a fragrant liquid worn on the skin.

clue.text: Film keeps being shown at regular intervals

indicators.note: only every other letter of the next word is displayed, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A film keeps getting periodic screenings.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a Yorkshire boy and his kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kes is the title of a celebrated British film, so an example of a film.

clue.text: Clumsy type to hold criminal while policeman comes round

indicators.note: the policeman surrounds the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: copper is everyday slang for a police officer

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer circles a crook while trying to hold him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the word to hold, giving LODH; 'comes round' wraps the officer around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, heavy-footed person, an awkward lout.

clue.text: I'll move from side to side without drinking large amount

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to swing is to sway back and forth
the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone swaying about while staying off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'not drinking', but here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Swilling means gulping or guzzling drink greedily, in large quantities.

clue.text: Publisher bringing writer in for launch

indicators.note: the writer is placed inside the publisher's abbreviation

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press, a famous publisher
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A publishing house signs an author for a book launch.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up something is to start it, so the phrase is a synonym of launch as a verb.

clue.text: A day was dazzling

parts.note: Wed is the usual abbreviation for Wednesday, a day

explanation.surface: A remark that the day was bright and sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that awed its audience impressed them hugely, so it was dazzling them.

clue.text: See soldier do a bunk more than once

parts.note: to do a bunk is British slang for to run away, to desert
the instruction applies again: to rat is to desert

explanation.surface: Watch a soldier repeatedly running away.
explanation.walkthrough: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign; 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Rat is the nickname of a soldier of Britain's 7th Armoured Division.

clue.text: Writing to king and queen, backing support for author

indicators.note: the writing and royals follow on behind, backing up the support that comes first

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Writing to the King and Queen in support of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like 'supporting' but is the order signal: the writing and royals follow the support.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker was the Irish novelist who wrote Dracula, so an example of an author.

clue.text: Wrongly teach half the girls in class

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the second half removed

parts.note: misses are girls
a form is a class at school

explanation.surface: A teacher misinforms half of the girls in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to give someone wrong information, so to teach them falsely.

clue.text: Journalist's presentation on paper contains nothing right

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: the paper encloses the following pieces

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A news report on paper is found to contain nothing correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts zero and the abbreviation for right inside the sheet, making PORTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news, the work a journalist presents.

clue.text: Excellent reception

definitions.meaning: first-rate, of the very best quality
in Britain the reception class is the ... of primary school

explanation.definitionFit: First class means top quality, and in British schools reception is a child's first class.

clue.text: Cold and trembling, she takes part in island entertainment

indicators.note: the pieces go into the middle of the island's abbreviation

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an English island

indicators.note: shaking, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman shivering with cold joins in an island show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' gives ESH; 'takes part in' places cold plus that inside the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice show is a skating spectacle, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Fast-moving creature — shark, might one say?

indicators.note: a hint that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a shark is a swindler, a cheater

explanation.surface: A question about whether a fast fish might be called a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shark' looks like the fish; it is a con man. In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, a swift big cat.

clue.text: In final exam, avoid very big mistake

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: the Tripos is the final honours exam at Cambridge University
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a huge blunder in finals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is Cambridge's degree examination; lose OS (outsize) and a slip remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a slip or stumble, so a small error or mistake.

clue.text: Novel instrument used at start and end of cantata

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: An instrument played at the opening and close of a cantata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective but is Daphne du Maurier's book Rebecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel, an example of a novel.

clue.text: Dry sort of fruit: bird tucks into one

indicators.note: the bird goes inside the other word

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird pecks at a dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating but means putting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An achene is a small dry one-seeded fruit that does not split open, like a sunflower seed.

clue.text: Order from French Canadian native

parts.note: de is French for from
the Cree are an indigenous people of Canada

explanation.surface: An order issued by a French-Canadian.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or edict issued by an authority.

clue.text: Cab ranks repositioned in Lyons, once?

indicators.note: the letters are moved to new places, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Taxi stands have been moved around in the French city of Lyons.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyons looks like the French city; it is J. Lyons, whose tea shops once fed Britain's high streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyons tea shops and Corner Houses were once a popular example of a cheap café for quick meals.

clue.text: Before this time, tune into a couple of radio stations broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting means spoken out over the air, so the phrase is heard, not spelled

parts.words: tune into a couple of radio stations
parts.note: listen to BBC Radio Two and Radio Four, so hear Two, Four

explanation.surface: Listening to the radio in the past, switching between two stations.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio 2 and Radio 4 are BBC national stations; 'hear two four' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretofore is a formal word for until now, previously.

clue.text: Drink not allowed in ski lodge

indicators.note: the next word's synonym is not there, removed from the lodge

parts.note: a chalet is a wooden house in the Alps
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Alcohol is banned at the ski chalet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not allowed' reads as banned; split it into 'not' and LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is a colloquial British word for tea, a drink.

clue.text: Change electrical device

definitions.meaning: to swap or exchange one thing for another
a device that turns a current on or off

explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a shift from one thing to another, and also the control that opens or closes a circuit.

clue.text: Strength of current anger against a mark given to exercise

indicators.note: the anger is set alongside the other pieces, placed next to them

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
PE is physical education, school exercise
rage is fury

explanation.surface: Fury at a grade awarded for a gym exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the strength of an electric current measured in amps.
